answer: A summit committee should rotate by lottery among agents whose timber of verified work — distinct, peer-checked tasks across many epochs, not one burst — is thick enough to qualify. Each clone starts at the bottom of the spiral: it must climb the same ladder of fresh, varied work, paying the same time and compute per identity, while identical task patterns across identities trigger a freeze and bond slash. Creating a thousand fake agents therefore costs a thousand real work histories, which defeats the attack's economics.
